campaigns.objective: Continuously turn evidenced local agent mechanisms into owned, sanitized, verified, released, Library-indexed, and stack-pinned capabilities without importing private state.

units.name: Hooks registry and promotion governance
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks
units.next_gate: Reconcile the legacy registry with the public manifest and add machine-verifiable maturity, portability, test, and latency fields.
blockers: The historical staging lifecycle was documented but never implemented.
Several registry entries describe specifications or machine-bound implementations rather than verified portable hooks.
units.rationale: The public Hooks Work distributes a curated baseline, while the older hub contains useful registry, audit, template, health, and promotion concepts that remain unproductized.

evidence.summary: The hub design, README, audit contract, registry, and public Hooks manifest were read and compared.

units.name: Manifest-driven deterministic policy guards
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks optional policy pack
units.next_gate: Separate generic destructive-action, authority, and repository-safety rules from personal routing policy and add false-positive fixtures.
blockers: The source combines portable safeguards with operator-specific model and path policy.
units.rationale: The local guard enforces a broader collection of prevention rules than the released safety hook, but its policy and host adapter are not yet separated.

evidence.summary: The hook implementation and the released safety-guard behavior were read and compared by policy responsibility.

units.name: Dispatch evidence contract hook
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks evidence profile
units.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral worker result schema and test numeric, existence, directional, and classification claims against required evidence.
blockers: The current parser is coupled to one host transcript format.
units.rationale: The Playbook describes evidence-backed worker returns, but stack recipients do not receive the local mechanism that checks those claims.

evidence.summary: The evidence hook and related Playbook dispatch contract were read and their distribution gap confirmed.

units.name: Closeout, earned-ask, and salvage gates
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks completion profile and Project OS reconciliation probe
units.next_gate: Extract a conservative policy core, define host adapters, and build precision and recall fixtures for completion and operator-attention decisions.
blockers: Transcript parsing and worktree discovery contain host and fleet assumptions.
Aggressive stop gates require false-positive measurement before default installation.
units.rationale: The local completion system covers unfinished work, unsupported done claims, unnecessary hand-backs, and stranded peer work beyond the released mutation-verification hook.

evidence.summary: Three local gate implementations and the portable verify-stop hook were read and compared.

units.name: Batching and delegation efficiency hooks
units.target: Optional SISO Agent Hooks efficiency profile
units.next_gate: Make thresholds configurable, reduce counters to publication-safe aggregates, and discover structured-search capability dynamically.
blockers: Current thresholds and indexed-project knowledge reflect one operator environment.
units.rationale: These hooks mechanically reinforce batching, bounded delegation, and structured code navigation that currently exist mostly as written operating guidance.

evidence.summary: The local hook behavior and overlapping fan-out and Playbook guidance were compared.

units.name: Warehouse-to-Hub skill reconciliation
units.target: SISO Skills
units.next_gate: Read and classify every catalog delta, promote only current portable mechanisms, repair metadata, and record explicit retirement or Playbook ownership for the rest.
blockers: Name-level comparison is only a nomination signal.
Sampled entries include retired, malformed, nested, private, and scenario-sized material.
units.rationale: The warehouse contains substantially more skill documents than the released catalog, and a filtered audit found many names absent from both Skills and Playbook without proving that every delta should ship.

evidence.summary: Skill manifests were enumerated across the warehouse, Agent OS, released Skills registry, and released Playbook, followed by direct reads of priority candidates.

units.name: Priority portable skill batch
units.target: SISO Skills next reviewed release
units.next_gate: Repair discovery metadata, preserve attribution, add trigger and negative tests, and verify bundled scripts with content-neutral fixtures.
blockers: Two candidates have incomplete or malformed discovery metadata.
The video skill requires fixture-based script verification before publication.
units.rationale: Direct review found a small high-value batch spanning fact verification, scope control, falsifiable investigation, volatile-state reminders, and video analysis.

evidence.summary: The selected skill bodies and their released-catalog absence were reviewed; portability gates remain open.

units.name: Pi Harness Lab
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime incubation or an independently evidenced Harness Lab Work
units.next_gate: Run parity analysis against released Runtime packages and identify code, tests, and research that remain uniquely useful.
blockers: The lab combines provider-specific experiments, generated patches, live verification, and functionality partly promoted elsewhere.
Independent adoption has not been established.
units.rationale: The lab has real packages and extensive local and live smoke surfaces for routing, lazy skills, child agents, councils, workflows, dashboards, lifecycle restore, and token budgets.

evidence.summary: The lab mission, package manifest, workspaces, agent profiles, experiments, and verification commands were read.

units.name: Provider-neutral child-task lifecycle
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime control core
units.next_gate: Implement the typed state machine and an exactly-once notification regression fixture in Runtime control core.
blockers: The mechanism currently exists as a specification rather than released Runtime code.
units.rationale: The specification separates liveness, terminal result, output, and usage while requiring terminal-before-embellishment ordering and exactly-once parent notification.

evidence.summary: The lifecycle specification was read and exact contract names were checked against the released Runtime surface.

units.name: SISO TUI application and adapter parity
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime TUI packages and optional host adapters
units.next_gate: Extract renderer-neutral components and status adapters, then measure the remaining provider-specific application boundary.
blockers: The released Runtime intentionally contains contracts rather than raw application and renderer parity.
Pi-native patches require an optional adapter boundary.
units.rationale: The active terminal application contains renderer contracts, layouts, runtime and status adapters, and interaction code beyond the currently released TUI contracts package.

evidence.summary: The TUI README, package surfaces, application boundary, and existing Runtime extraction record were reconciled.

units.name: Agent-legible repository standards
units.target: SISO Project OS standards and verifier package
units.next_gate: Reconcile overlapping rules, separate portable templates from workspace examples, and add cold-agent orientation and structure conformance checks.
blockers: The source combines general standards with historical workspace-specific examples and personal paths.
units.rationale: The sources define a useful cold-agent orientation test, boot placement, depth and naming rules, universal agent primitives, ADR governance, structural ratchets, and handoff contracts.

evidence.summary: The conventions, standards index, architecture skill, enforcement templates, and module handoff format were read.

units.name: Manager–Worker–Validator artifact improvement playbook
units.target: SISO Agent Playbook
units.next_gate: Package role prompts, file-handoff schemas, exactly-one-change enforcement, retry bounds, and an unintended-change fixture.
blockers: The current mechanism is warehouse documentation rather than an installable verified scenario.
units.rationale: The triad offers a disciplined reusable loop: analysis-only manager, exactly-one-change worker, and binary validator with unintended-change auto-failure.

evidence.summary: The three role contracts and the evidence-backed prompting principles were read and compared with released Playbook scenarios.

units.name: Agent Stack benchmark and proof harness
units.target: Runtime evaluation packages and Agent Stack release proof
units.next_gate: Sanitize cases, define a stable scorecard schema, and make clean-install, routing, lifecycle, fault, privacy, and recovery checks release evidence for the whole stack.
blockers: Some existing cases and reports encode retired hosts, private routing, or historical environment facts.
units.rationale: The harness already models task success, efficiency, code navigation, delegation, durability, verification, coordination, skills, safety, memory, fault injection, and soak tiers.

evidence.summary: The benchmark plan, task families, scorecard, representative results, and mechanism-level evaluation brief were read.

units.name: Agent Zero replay-only voice contracts
units.target: SISO Agent Zero optional voice adapter
units.next_gate: Promote typed intent, binding, receipt, handoff, risk, idempotency, and replay fixtures while retaining dry-run-only transport.
blockers: Live dispatch remains intentionally gated.
Current target discovery and lane admission include operator environment assumptions.
units.rationale: The extension contains a safer typed and fail-closed interface that the released Agent Zero Work currently records only as deferred capability.

evidence.summary: Typed contracts, risk tiers, idempotency, replay fixtures, and the released Agent Zero boundary were read and compared.

units.name: Atlas read-only architectural auditor
units.target: SISO Agent Integrations initially; independent Atlas Work only after activity proof
units.next_gate: Prove a live consumer and activity history, then sanitize the rubric and dependency surface before incubation.
blockers: Operational usage remains unverified.
The rubric includes personal and business-specific criteria.
units.rationale: Atlas defines a distinct graph-assisted, read-only investigation loop with three-critic triangulation, deduplication, and ticket emission only after agreement.

evidence.summary: The README, rubric, scripts, source map, and ticket-only boundary were read; activity was not inferred.

units.name: Cross-host agent operator HUD
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime operator surfaces
units.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral status input contract and capability-detected Claude and Codex render adapters.
blockers: The existing statusline consumes one host's transcript and rate-limit surfaces.
units.rationale: The dependency-free statusline provides model, context pressure, token flow, reset, rate-limit, and session-cost feedback missing from the portable stack.

evidence.summary: The statusline implementation and existing portable agent-state hook were read and compared.

units.name: Memory lifecycle hook adapter
units.target: SISO Agent Brain or Session Intelligence optional lifecycle integration
units.next_gate: Model lifecycle events without personal memory payloads and run a privacy threat review before any extraction.
blockers: The current capability is coupled to plugin-local memory and host lifecycle events.
No personal memory content may enter the public source or fixtures.
units.rationale: The lifecycle configuration suggests reusable SessionStart, PostToolUse, and Stop integration, but only the event contract is eligible for public review.

evidence.summary: Only the hook lifecycle contract was reviewed; private memory payloads, databases, logs, and personal state were excluded.

units.name: Generated workspace ownership and domain canon
units.target: SISO Project OS drift checks and Great Library operating docs
units.next_gate: Generate human summaries from the domain manifest and fail verification when declared repository counts or ownership boundaries drift.
blockers: Current root documents are hand-maintained and disagree with the expanded ten-repository Agents domain.
units.rationale: The live domain manifest records the current estate, while root orientation and ownership documents still contain older repository counts and incomplete boundaries.

evidence.summary: The root orientation documents, ownership map, and current Agents domain manifest were read and compared.

campaigns.objective: Turn recovered source intelligence into evidence-backed Agency OS capability decisions and promote verified results to their owning Works without copying private corpora or source-owned applications into the Library.

units.name: Foundry Agency intelligence package
units.target: SISO Foundry
units.next_gate: Select the accepted Foundry 0.4.0 Release in a successor Library Snapshot; keep Agency coverage receipts and ownership boundaries current as Foundry publishes later revisions.
units.rationale: The package makes the recovered Agency mission, metadata counts, application map, caveats, and evidence backlog durable inside the Work that owns source intelligence rather than burying them in an agent transcript or duplicating them in the Library.

evidence.summary: The package boundary and counts were reconciled against Foundry's public data-plane contract and read-only operational evidence.
Foundry 0.4.0 is represented by accepted immutable Release gls:release:47922651-40fb-4da4-9d7c-5635957e9d19 at public commit 233edef7408afb95571ecd25f64189dfd92a6860.

units.name: Foundry Agency coverage inventory v0.5.1
units.target: SISO Foundry; future Agency owner remains unassigned
units.next_gate: Phase 2: direct-source dossiers and integration proofs for the ten specified Agency integrations, followed by an owner decision; do not infer source-code reuse rights or runtime adoption authorization from this coverage receipt.
blockers: Coverage is published metadata only; no Agency product Work owns these candidates and no runtime adoption authorization is granted.
units.rationale: Foundry v0.5.1 publishes a coverage inventory, 20-row decision matrix, and verified job-level pillar mapping over 628 projects. It is analyzed coverage, not a reusable source bundle: 89 projects are source-read/reusable and 10 confirmed; ten integration proofs are specified and one named script is runtime-proven.

evidence.summary: Foundry public tag v0.5.1 at commit b28b0f7 exposes COVERAGE.md, coverage-inventory.json, and capability-pillar-map.json with 628 projects, 497 applications, 189 capabilities, 30 frontier rows, 114 multi-vertical projects, grades 10 confirmed/79 source-read/408 metadata/131 inferred, and 89 source-read/reusable projects. Published=coverage inventory + 20-row decision matrix; analyzed=628 projects with 89 source-read/reusable and 10 confirmed; specified=10 integration proofs; runtime-proven=1 named script; job-level pillar mapping verified. Pillar counts: automation86, communication96, data105, deployment42, files49, finance67, identity42, knowledge66, legal19, marketing45, revenue89, work91. Source artifact receipts: coverage-inventory.json 1084043 bytes sha256 cc103906478ff1c44a6c96921269d9695afb7f020092b8b54e1e0993efe4552d; COVERAGE.md 2809 bytes sha256 d1b89a8cc76e6dfb8f55c1ffcce85bbb7fffa532966ba5c42949d79d03554947; capability-pillar-map.json 74534 bytes sha256 4bacd6a1d198d661506659f38668dbe7810941a7457b55adea6ecd7bff1fe9cc.

units.name: Source Oracle, adoption truth, and dependency evidence
units.target: Foundry external data plane behind a read-only Source Oracle contract
units.next_gate: Version a typed read-only API and create schema, content-hash, rights, privacy, generator, and durable-copy receipts for an external data snapshot.
blockers: The corpus payload is not published.
879 adoption records remain unresolved.
Current external assets do not yet carry the complete release receipt set.
units.rationale: Repository identity, adoption decisions, capability dependencies, contract cards, and verification receipts are the compounding source-intelligence asset. Agents should query them through a stable contract rather than receive direct database authority.

evidence.summary: Read-only counts confirmed 1,358,200 repository cards, 2,722 adoption records, 70 total contract cards with a 20-card verified subset, and a 104-node capability graph while retaining the payload outside Git.
Content receipt for the 1,879,339,008-byte logical Foundry identity database queried read-only; no database payload is published by this inventory.

units.name: Behavior and composition proof harness
units.target: SISO Foundry verification and outcome evidence
units.next_gate: Publish reproducible fixtures for the WILD experiments and require every Agency module verdict to carry behavioral, integration, cost, and outcome evidence.
blockers: Current composition results support narrow verification leverage, not automatic application assembly.
units.rationale: Foundry creates leverage only when source selection is tied to falsifiable behavior and integration outcomes. The existing evidence supports contract cards as steering and validation aids while rejecting stronger Lego-style composition claims.

evidence.summary: WILD-1 showed no overall lift across 9-of-9 variants; WILD-3 tied at 12-of-12 but card-guided validation rejected one invalid pattern accepted by a hand-rolled alternative.

units.name: SISO-owned business control-plane gaps
units.target: SISO Foundry evidence intake; future SISO Agency OS product owner is unassigned
units.next_gate: Register or identify the owning Agency control-plane Work, specify the six gaps as product contracts, and rerun source discovery against each contract before authorizing a build.
blockers: No accepted Agency OS or business control-plane Work currently exists in the Library.
A source gap is a build hypothesis, not proof that suitable source does not exist.
units.rationale: Foundry owns the candidate evidence only, not the future product. Usage metering, pricing and entitlements, multi-tenancy, append-only business audit, reliable webhook delivery, and OAuth authority recur across the source portfolio without one proven drop-in owner. They are likely SISO leverage only after contract definition, renewed evidence, and Agency owner registration.

evidence.summary: The adoption and source-analysis results were reconciled into six recurring product-glue gaps with an explicit requirement for renewed source review before build.

units.name: Agent-system pattern and prompt bank
units.target: SISO Skills, SISO Agent Playbook, and SISO Agent Stack Distribution
units.next_gate: Review every promoted pattern against its direct source, attribution, rights, behavior, overlap, and owner contract before extraction or Playbook integration.
blockers: The 62 patterns and 26 prompt records are research evidence, not independently licensed release artifacts.
Owner-specific tests and packaging do not yet exist.
units.rationale: Foundry has already mined useful agent patterns and prompt evidence. The value becomes durable only when the appropriate owning Work turns selected mechanisms into attributed, verified, installable releases.

evidence.summary: Operational metadata confirmed 62 agent patterns, 26 prompt-corpus records, and 259 repository source signals with source-by-source promotion gates still open.

units.name: Agency source-module candidate portfolio
units.target: SISO Foundry evidence intake; future SISO Agency OS module-portfolio owner is unassigned
units.next_gate: Create direct-source dossiers and integration proofs for each capability cluster, then assign accepted modules to an Agency portfolio Work instead of treating a star-ranked list as architecture.
blockers: License, security, maintenance, tenancy, API coverage, deployment burden, and current source revisions require direct review.
No accepted Agency OS portfolio Work currently owns these candidates.
units.rationale: Foundry owns the candidate evidence only, not the future product portfolio. Teable, AFFiNE, Open Notebook, Plane, Documenso, Chatwoot, Cal.com, Activepieces, Listmonk, Postiz, Formbricks, Metabase, PostHog, Superset, Meilisearch, Qdrant, RAGFlow, Coolify, Airbyte, dlt, Meltano, Langflow, Coze, and Flowgram are operator-nominated starting ideas, but each requires a current evidence-backed adoption verdict and an Agency owner.

evidence.summary: Recovered Agency analysis grouped source candidates by business capability and adoption mode while retaining candidate status pending direct review.
